title: TomoClub | Game-Based Learning, Live (TAICY 2026 Round 2) | Parent Highlight
notes: Times are seconds into the source recording. Cut points come from word-level timestamps (faster-whisper, checked against the audio energy), padded into the silence between words.

video_in: the clip's picture comes from that time instead (B-roll from the same round). Used for the Game 1 debrief, where the screen share shows a 'DEFEAT' results screen we don't want to put on a child.
layout: 'gallery' clips get the Zoom name labels blurred (privacy_blur.gallery, source pixels at 2560x1440).

Captions are clean verbatim: filler words removed, meaning unchanged. A line that three speech models heard three different ways (38:33, 'what happens if all three of us ... together?') is left out rather than guessed.
Students are identified by first name only.

1.title: Think it through
1.sub: Game 1: a strategy game with no rulebook

2.title: Win as a team
2.sub: Game 2: a co-op puzzle they can only solve together

sequence.speaker: VK, TomoClub facilitator
sequence.text: We don't give you any rules.

sequence.speaker: VK, TomoClub facilitator
sequence.text: You have to talk to each other and figure it out.

sequence.speaker: Student
sequence.text: Communication is key.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: Think about… do you want to go aggressive, or do you want to go passive?

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: What did you do differently? What changed, and what was your thought process or strategy?

sequence.speaker: Vedant
sequence.text: In this round, instead of trying to directly attack, I tried to surround his entire territory from the sides as well, so that one click can take a larger portion out of it.

sequence.speaker: Sudeep
sequence.text: I tried to click on the triangles which made more hexagons, but a lot of hexagons were spawning at once and I didn't understand what was happening. So I just didn't know what to do.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: No problem. That's the part of learning, right? You don't know, so you experiment with different things.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: So you can always bounce back in this game, right? And Sudeep, I saw you doing it. So, good job.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: In this game, you will be playing as a team. Now I want to see how you're going to crack this game as a team.

sequence.speaker: Live gameplay
sequence.text: Actually, I'll just be at the button, unlocking the doors you explore, through each door.

sequence.speaker: Student
sequence.text: And also, each person handling a separate responsibility means that you don't have to shuffle between places and waste time.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: Yeah, exactly. That's right, so you can optimize for resources and efficiency.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: How are you judging whether you're communicating efficiently or not?

sequence.speaker: Student
sequence.text: Being able to get our thoughts to the other person, like, to make them understand what we need.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: When I'm asking you a question, you both are listening to me.

sequence.speaker: Student
sequence.text: Yeah, we need to be able to listen to the other person as well.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: Yes, communication is a two-way street. You need to give space. You need to take space.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: Why are you doing it so fast? How are you doing it so fast?

sequence.speaker: Student
sequence.text: Because we remember where all the circuit pieces are, and exactly what we should do at which time.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: 45 seconds, you've completed it. Pretty cool.

stat.label: Same level, lights off:
stat.note: to clear it, using the map and roles they had worked out in earlier rounds.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: This is called embracing the chaos. When something is put at you, you're not going to panic. That's what happens in life. Life gives us situations and challenges, right?

sequence.speaker: Vedant
sequence.text: I found the game pretty fun. It's quite unique. Usually in other games you're competing against someone, but here you're actually working together for a certain goal, which was nice, and it was fun to play.

sequence.speaker: Sudeep
sequence.text: And this game also includes a lot of trial and error to actually learn the rules. For example, once we went to the platform but realized that we did not have all the circuit pieces needed.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: That's the key, right? The whole point of game-based learning is you figure out the rules. Because figuring out is an aspect of life. You need to figure out things.

sequence.speaker: VK
sequence.text: So these are just skills that, when honed time and again, you get better at. So don't stop with this session. Keep honing more.
